title: Great focused tool, one minor gripe: surface the Notes, please
body:
I have been using Productive for about 2 years and I find its focus on repeating habits generallywell thought out. I use it most days for key reminders. The interface is clear and easy to use. I think for the vast majority of people looking for a habit tracker, it’s great. 

The one minor criticism is that in a recent update, the Notes field has gotten buried in the interface and I have to work consciously to find it. 

I might be an edge case, but I use the Notes field for several of my habits to review key aspects of the habit. For example, I keep a daily habit of reviewing people in my life who have some sort of challenge: I want to see their name and their challenge so I can decide if I need to check in or do something. 

To get to the Notes field now I have to make 3 presses: 

1. Click on the Habit detail (>).
2. I have to look around the details page, see nothing that looks like a note, and remember to click on the ellipsis (...) on the upper right of the screen.
3. Click the Notes icon. 

That’s 3 clicks and several seconds of having to remember where to look for the notes. I wish the Notes were surfaced more easily, such as 

One other minor observation: when I have a Notes field visible, the new interface with the big blue + symbol obscures the last line or two of the notes: I have to physically drag the note upward to be able to see the last two lines, then they spring back below the blue + symbol. This seems intrusive and counter-productive to me: if I open the notes, I want to see the notes. 

I think if the Notes interface issues I outline above were fixed, I’d give this application 5 stars.

Thanks.

title: Needs more control over settings
body:
I’ve been a user for years. The newest update that nags me every time I try to mark a habit as failed for the day (pop up: “Are you sure the day is over?” with a comment box) is annoying and infantilizing. Yes, I am sure the day is over. I’m doing my daily cleanup. Leave me alone! Let me turn this feature off, PLEASE. May need to find a new app otherwise. I’m not expecting perfection from every habit, every day, and I don’t need the guilt trip from the app about that.

Edited to add: I do see that the developer usually responds to reviews, which I appreciate. But I am not open to submitting a feature request or sending screen recordings. You already know how the feature works; your PM (or someone) chose not to prioritize building an off switch for it despite it being a predictably disruptive feature. Shipping annoying stuff without an off switch is a churn risk, and I shouldn’t need to find an issue to upvote to tell you that.

title: Very useful
body: I've been using this just over a month now and I find it to be a very useful tool. It's designed with the user in mind. I like the display and that i can see my goals on the one screen. I can update the status of the goals on the screen and I can add notes on the one screen. I like the notes button where for each goal it displays all notes written in chronological (descending ) order. It's very well thought out. They've kept UI simple and easy on the eye too. Great!! After it updated all my data was still there-phew !! I like simple, good looking and practical - this app ticks all of these requirements. It's helping me track where I'm at. I really like the skip option - as I don't train everyday and ticking skip rather than no is great for motivation! When I do actually accidentally miss a goal I click no but choosing to skip a day as part of maintaining recovery period and having a sensible app that knows about skip is terrific. Definitely recommend!!

title: Good app, easy to use… few details could make it dynamite
body:
Just a few details could make even another step easier to use. 1-call the list of goals something besides a journal. “Journal” as a title if a group of goals isn’t proper use of the word journal. 2-repeat tapping on a goal should cycle the response if checkmark, x , skip, and blank, rather than having to move your finger to click on the icon (both should work). 3-when tapping on the icon response, default next action be the next goal, same date, if the date being recorded is today. If I am recording yesterday’s performance and click on X or checkmark, or Skip, the default should advance the mark (cursor to today… staying on the same goal.
4-if a NOTE has been created for a goal and a date, there should be some sort of badge or marker or shaded or outlined; as is, it is hard to see which goals and on which days there is a note.
These tweeks would make this App another big step better. I think the programmer has moved on and hasn’t modified or updated this App for quite awhile… but still is good!

title: Best habit app, supportive developers, love it!
body:
I reckon I’ve tried almost every habit tracking app on the App Store, and this is the one I’ve settled on.  I’ve been using it for a year now and still happy as.  

For one, I love the fact that I can use it not just as a habit tracker but also a place to keep notes of things I’ve done (for example, when I mark exercise as done, I can put details of the exercise), and then I can review those notes (filtered by activity, or category, or just see all of them) in a diary-like view. To me this is gold, and the best implementation I’ve seen of this feature. In fact, I requested some changes to make it easier to see and edit notes attached to a habit, and the developer implemented what I asked and more - he pretty much filled all the gaps I identified. How good is that!?  

The reporting views (by week/ month/ year) are a delight, and checking off tasks as done is quick and easy (including adding notes).  

Only improvement I’ve not yet seen is the ability to mark a task as done for the day if it’s an x number per week or month (like a max number per day count).. so I can see if I’ve done something today without clicking into it and looking at the calendar.. but that’s a small inconvenience that I’m quite happy to live with.

Get this app - you won’t be disappointed.

title: Good, but needs to be polished
body:
I have the premium version, and I think it’s well worth it. However, I have some suggestions because this app could use some polish.

First, when you add a note to a habit to appear under the habit name, the text is always white. Because of this, its either barely visible or invisible because the colors of uncompleted tasks are too light. Furthermore, the color of the text for the habit name is always black. So when you complete a task and the color darkens, it becomes much less visible.

What this means is that your “Today” page will often look like a mess. Some text stands out, some is invisible, and it all looks frankly unpolished and ugly. This is disappointing because this page is the one you use most.

Another problem is the “Habit Tracker” calendar page. Frankly, it looks bad. There’s no other way to say it. The 6 available “Report Styles” all look juvenile and cluttered. Everything on the calendar feels small and cramped, and scrolling from week to week is a chore because of those tiny arrow buttons. This could be fixed by simply getting rid of that big “Habit Tracker” label on the top, and shrinking the stats at the bottom.

I want to love this app, but I can’t. Not yet. I’ll keep using it for now, but unless the UI doesn’t improve, I will probably eventually leave. I really would prefer a sleeker, more minimalistic, more professional looking app. I hope you take these comments into consideration, because I really do like this product but it definitely needs some improvement.
